test_title: RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-II Official Paper (Held On: 20 Dec, 2025)
subject: general
question: In what ratio must Rohit, a grocer, mix two varieties of gram flour costing ₹130 and ₹150 per kg, respectively, so as to get a mixture worth ₹145.50 per kg?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Using the direct rule of alligation method for mixing two varieties:

Quantity Ratio = (Cost of Variety 2 − Mean Price) : (Mean Price − Cost of Variety 1)

Quantity Ratio = (150 − 145.50) : (145.50 − 130)

Quantity Ratio = 4.50 : 15.50

Quantity Ratio = 45 : 155 = 9 : 31

**∴ The correct answer is 9 : 31.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Cost of variety 1 (C₁) = ₹130 per kg

Cost of variety 2 (C₂) = ₹150 per kg

Mean price of the mixture (M) = ₹145.50 per kg

 
• 
• 
• 
• 130 150 145.50 4.50 15.50 Variety 1 Variety 2 Mean Price Ratio = 4.50 : 15.50 

**Formula Used:**

Let the quantities of variety 1 and variety 2 be x and y respectively.

Weighted Average Price = (C₁ × x + C₂ × y) ÷ (x + y)

**Calculations:**

⇒ (130 × x + 150 × y) ÷ (x + y) = 145.50

⇒ 130x + 150y = 145.50(x + y)

⇒ 130x + 150y = 145.50x + 145.50y

⇒ 150y − 145.50y = 145.50x − 130x

⇒ 4.50y = 15.50x

⇒ x ÷ y = 4.50 ÷ 15.50

⇒ x ÷ y = 450 ÷ 1550

⇒ x ÷ y = 45 ÷ 155 = 9 ÷ 31

⇒ x : y = 9 : 31

**∴ The correct answer is 9 : 31.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Rule of Alligation

When two ingredients of different prices are mixed, the ratio of their quantities is inversely proportional to the differences in their prices from the mean price. Ratio = (C₂ − M) : (M − C₁).

Weighted Average

It is used to find the average of two or more groups when their quantities and individual averages are known. Formula: Aw = (n₁A₁ + n₂A₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂).

Replacement Method in Mixtures

If a container initially holds x units of pure liquid, and y units are drawn out and replaced with water n times, the final quantity of pure liquid remaining is: Final = x × (1 − y ÷ x)ⁿ.
